restrictions: The online algorithm is deterministic replay of exactly the two 128-byte messages in proof.md; it is not a submitted generator for new collisions.
The selected target has the standard fixed SHA-256 IV, original round indices 0 through 30 on every padded block, full eight-word feed-forward, FIPS padding, and all 256 output bits.

All historical characteristic search, failed work, table generation, matching, construction, and checking are charged once as preprocessing and included in total time; no cross-target amortization is claimed.

Declared time_log2=49.81 anchors H-HISTORICAL-TIME on the EUROCRYPT 2024 published complete constructive complexity 2^49.8 as the preprocessing upper bound, plus a negligible online term; it deliberately refuses the knife-edge ASIACRYPT matching-phase headline 2^40.5.
The score is conditional on H-HISTORICAL-TIME and H-HISTORICAL-MEMORY; neither bound has an authoritative organizer-model trace or resource receipt.

The organizer experiment checks only the exact collision relation. Repeated replay rows do not measure success probability, expected work, preprocessing, memory, novelty, or generator reproducibility.
This exploratory package claims no new cryptanalysis, no full-SHA-256 or 32-round collision, no lower security bound, and no rigorous qualification.
Under collision-frontier-v5 the scored scalar is time_log2 only; memory is reported and reviewed but does not enter the scalar.
baseline_improved names the required nominal reference identifier and does not assert a proved cryptanalytic improvement over that nominal.

heuristics.statement: All computational work that led to the fixed witness, including differential-trail discovery, SAT/SMT and other tool runs, failed or abandoned trials, table construction, matching, message construction, serialization, verification, and the publisher's disclosed additional experiments, is at most 2^49.8 collision-frontier-v5 charged target-compression units (the Li-Liu-Wang EUROCRYPT 2024 published complete constructive complexity); total time after deterministic replay is less than 2^49.81 units.
heuristics.scope: Exactly the fixed two-message 31-round-prefix SHA-256 collision in proof.md, with all one-time historical construction paid once and no amortization across targets or outputs.
heuristics.extrapolation: The preprocessing envelope is exactly the EUROCRYPT 2024 published complete constructive complexity 2^49.8 for ordinary 31-step SHA-256 collisions, with no extra additive margin on that figure. Online cost is bounded by 2^20 + 6 compression-equivalents, so 2^49.8 + 2^20 + 6 has log2 about 49.8000000015 < 49.81. The ASIACRYPT 2024 matching-phase headline 2^40.5 and 1.2-hour/64-thread run remain supporting evidence that a cheaper matching engine exists inside that envelope; they are not treated as a complete all-history ledger. Publication units are charged as target-compression equivalents with no 1/2140 word-op discount.
heuristics.limitations: No immutable job ledger, instruction trace, immutable practical-generator build, or organizer-unit conversion receipt is available in the public sources used here. If characteristic search plus all omitted experiments truly exceeded 2^49.8 compression-equivalents, preprocessing_log2=49.8, time_log2=49.81, and the score fail while the collision itself remains valid. This package deliberately refuses knife-edge claims near 2^40.5-2^41 for that reason. Declaring 49.81 rather than 50 only removes the previous 0.1-bit padding above 2^49.8; it does not newly rely on the ASIACRYPT matching headline.

heuristics.statement: Peak simultaneously retained storage over every historical construction phase and deterministic replay is less than 2^30 bytes, including code, advice, tables, indices, messages, thread state, constants, allocator overhead, solver and tool state, and other working storage.
heuristics.scope: Exactly the construction history and replay of the fixed witness in proof.md, including characteristic search and all practical-attack phases rather than only the final online program.
heuristics.extrapolation: The ASIACRYPT slides report about 2^19.8 ten-word tuples. A packed 40-byte representation is about 2^25.12 bytes. The submitted 2^30 cap leaves more than an order of magnitude of headroom above that raw table for indices, code, allocator state, workers, SAT/SMT state, and other peaks. Memory is reported only under v5 and does not enter the scored scalar.
heuristics.limitations: Public figures count entries, not peak RSS. A compatible layout is not proof of the layout used historically. If any historical charged phase reaches 2^30 bytes, the memory claim fails. Because memory is unscored under v5, a memory-only failure does not by itself change time_log2, but it is still a reviewed metric and a declared bound.
